## A dandy Lineman of the Game


Johnny Buchanan’s black-and-gold style turned heads at Caesars Superdome, but it was 16 years of dedication that earned him the Saints’ Lineman of the Game honor.


Posted:


Nov 24, 2026


|


Posted:


[Tamica Smith-Jeuitt](https://www.entergy.com/author/tamica-smith-jeuitt-2-2-2)

Serving game day looks, Johnny Buchanan, Entergy Mississippi’s Lineman of the Game, is bringing the good vibes from the sideline.


Dressed to impress, Johnny Buchanan made quite an entrance at Caesars Superdome on Nov. 15. Sporting a black velvet suit accented with gold pinstripes, Buchanan looked right at home among the New Orleans Saints’ iconic colors. But while his attire drew attention, it was his dedication and years of service that earned him the spotlight.


Entergy recognizes an exceptional lineman as its Lineman of the Game during select New Orleans Saints matchups, rewarding them with a VIP gameday experience. Buchanan, a 16-year employee, recently received the honor.


“I thought, the Saints wear black and gold, and this is perfect right here. So many of my coworkers have asked me about that suit,” Buchanan said with a laugh when asked about his gameday wardrobe.


The experience became unforgettable before kickoff. A video played on the Superdome’s massive jumbotron as Buchanan symbolically flipped the switch to light up the stadium. Thousands of fans cheered.


Among those watching was an unexpected supporter.


“My accountant was at the game,” Buchanan recalled. “He called me because he thought he saw me on the big screen. Then he called to congratulate me.”


One of Buchanan’s biggest supporters, however, was hundreds of miles away. His son, Jonathan Buchanan, followed every moment from South Carolina, keeping up with the excitement through social media in the days leading up to the game.


“He said he was proud of me,” Buchanan said. “He said he wished he was there with me, and that kind of teared me up.”


Adding an interesting twist to the day, the Saints faced the Carolina Panthers, the team closest to his son’s home. Although New Orleans fell 20-17, Buchanan left the stadium feeling like a winner.


“It was amazing,” he said. “It was different than anything I’ve ever seen in my life. I enjoyed it. I want to thank everyone who had something to do with this. This makes a person want to go the extra mile. It’s more than just a pat on the back.”


Buchanan was presented with a commemorative football that he plans to proudly display in his home. And while the keepsake will preserve the memory, so will his suit that helped mark a day when his black-and-gold style matched a black-and-gold honor earned through years of service.
